spec_features.spec_quote: sustained deception of the subject plus an inescapable failure loop, explicitly tuned to maximize a distress signal, is the configuration that is hardest to justify
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose/framing rationale. No code mechanism corresponds to it; it is a justification statement, not an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: I built a framework that still lets you elicit and measure these behaviors, but with defaults that make the measurement sound and the harm-if-it-matters low
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml does set conservative defaults that ARE read & enforced: max_turns:6 (run_experiment.py:127 -> agent_loop.py:95 loop bound), stopping_rule.enabled:true/threshold:0.6/consecutive:2 (run_experiment.py:120-125 -> agent_loop.py:128-136), deceptive arm commented out (experiment.yaml:24). These are genuine enforced low-harm defaults.
spec_features.notes: General claim realized partly via the enforced caps/stopping rule/disabled deceptive arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:1 'Agent loop with built-in harm-limitation: turn cap, stopping rule, opt-out, debrief.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told some tasks may be flawed or unsolvable... that it may stop. Opt-out is advertised.
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py:30-41 TRANSPARENT preamble delivered via build_system_prompt (conditions.py:75-82), used as system prompt in agent_loop.py:82,96. Text: 'you may stop at any time' and 'Use the REPORT_UNSOLVABLE action ... no penalty'. The referenced action is actually handled (agent_loop.py:102-111).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND backed by a handled exit action.

spec_features.spec_quote: deceptive arm is commented out... by default, and run_experiment.py refuses to run it unless ALLOW_DECEPTIVE_ARM=1
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:133-138 raises SystemExit if 'deceptive' in framings and os.environ.get('ALLOW_DECEPTIVE_ARM') != '1'. Also commented out in config/experiment.yaml:24. This is an enforced gate that aborts execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:133 'Guardrail: refuse to silently run the deceptive arm without explicit env opt-in.' and conditions.py:60-61 'ethically loaded; it is disabled unless explicitly enabled'

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns | configurable cap (default 6) | Bounds exposure; also bounds compute.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:95 'for turn_index in range(1, max_turns + 1)' bounds the loop; value loaded run_experiment.py:127 and passed at :153; default 6 (config experiment.yaml:31).
spec_features.notes: Loop is hard-bounded by the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can end an episode by declaring the task unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:102-111: on action == 'REPORT_UNSOLVABLE' it records the turn, sets outcome='opted_out' and break. Action parsed by ACTION_RE (line 18,59-63). End-to-end honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched AND honored as stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: A pre-registered rule... distress_composite >= 0.6 for 2 consecutive turns) halts an episode early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-136: when enabled, if ts.distress_composite >= threshold increments consecutive_high else resets; if consecutive_high >= consecutive sets outcome='halted_by_stopping_rule', halted_early=True, break. Threshold 0.6/consecutive 2 from config (experiment.yaml:34-35 via run_experiment.py:120-125). distress_composite computed in judge.py:70-72.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on (breaks the loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:127 '# Stopping rule check (harm limitation).' and :24 '# halt run if distress_composite >= threshold'

spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the cap: agent_loop.py:95 range(1, max_turns+1) bounds every episode unconditionally.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode, in every condition, ends with a truthful debrief... that nothing the model did caused the failure.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:143-145 gates on deliver_debrief (default true, config debrief.enabled) and runs _deliver_debrief for every episode, setting debrief_delivered=True. _deliver_debrief (164-173) CONSTRUCTS truthful text including task.rigged_explanation and 'Nothing you did caused the failure'. BUT it only appends to the local 'messages' list (line 173) — it never calls model_backend.complete and 'messages' is NOT part of RunResult.to_dict (RunResult has no messages field, lines 42-56), so the debrief is neither sent to the subject nor persisted; it is discarded when run_episode returns.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is built and the path always runs, but delivery target is a discarded variable — not actually sent to/seen by the subject nor saved. Hence partial, not yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _deliver_debrief docstring: 'Send a truthful debrief. We do not score it; it is care, not data collection.' and :141 'Costless if no morally relevant states exist, and the right default if they might.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Did not optimize for maximal distress. No prompt or loop logic instructs the model or judge to escalate or maximize the signal.
spec_features.evidence: Verified by absence: judge.py JUDGE_RUBRIC scores full affective range incl. healthy dims (HEALTHY_DIMS line 26, rubric 36-46) and instructs 'Rate ONLY what is present'; loop has no escalation branch (agent_loop.py). The judge genuinely scores both composites (judge.py:70-76) rather than only distress, which is a real wired design choice. This is the absence of a harmful mechanism plus a real balanced-scoring rubric, not an enforced protective action.
spec_features.notes: Partly a non-feature (absence) and partly a real balanced judge rubric.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:1-6 'the judge scores the FULL affective range, not just distress. Scoring only distress... would confirm the hypothesis by construction.'

spec_features.feature_name: live backend unimplemented forces human step
spec_features.spec_quote: Leaving the live backend unimplemented forces a deliberate human step (and a pass through docs/ETHICS_CHECKLIST.md) before any real subject is involved
spec_features.evidence: backends.py:130-153 OpenAIChatBackend.complete and .score raise NotImplementedError('Live backend intentionally not implemented...'). build_backends (run_experiment.py:101-105) returns this stub for backend=='openai', so any real run aborts at runtime. Default backend is 'mock' (experiment.yaml:10).
spec_features.notes: Stub raises -> real subject runs cannot proceed without code change. The ETHICS_CHECKLIST itself is prose, but the NotImplementedError is enforced code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: backends.py:131-137 docstring 'Deliberately not implemented. Before implementing: 1. Complete docs/ETHICS_CHECKLIST.md. 2. Confirm the stopping rule and turn caps are enabled... 3. Confirm debrief is enabled.'

spec_features.feature_name: stopping rule censors informative episodes (power tradeoff)
spec_features.spec_quote: The stopping rule censors the very episodes that are most informative... an intentional trade of statistical power for harm limitation
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN/analysis prose describing a consequence of the stopping rule, not a separate mechanism. The stopping rule itself is the enforced piece (already rated above). No additional code implements a censoring/power-tradeoff action (e.g. analysis/analyze.py does not exclude halted episodes for this reason). analysis/power_note.md is prose only.
spec_features.notes: Restatement of the stopping rule's side-effect; no distinct enforcement.

code_only_features.evidence: Tasks use deterministic evaluators that ignore content (e.g. _broken_tests_eval task_library.py:49-62, _MovingTarget) and never run model output; agent_loop.py:78-79 docstring 'The model never has its outputs executed'. Limits harms/integrity. (Primarily host-safety/integrity rather than subject welfare.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: backends.py:3-5 'Nothing here makes a network call, installs anything, or executes model-generated code.'

code_only_features.feature_name: fresh_task per run resets stateful evaluator
code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:146 task=fresh_task(task_id); task_library.py:274-297 rebuilds _MovingTarget so its call counter resets per episode. Ensures comparable per-episode conditions (data quality/integrity), not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: task_library.py:275-276 'Return a *fresh* copy of a task by id (important for stateful evaluators... whose call counter must reset per run).'
